subject: Re: SDK parity rollout — release messaging + semver (defaults vs flags)
body:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Cho <henry@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:18 AM PT
Subject: SDK parity rollout — release messaging + semver (defaults vs flags)

Henry — we need to land on a clear stance this week so the SDK leads can stop thrashing.

Open questions:
1) Semver: do we treat changes to retry/timeout defaults + streaming disconnect handling as “breaking” (major) or “behavioral but within expectations” (minor)?
2) Gating: do we ship new behavior as defaults, or gate behind a config flag / env var (and for how long)?
3) Messaging: how do we explain this without scaring existing customers (esp the folks who already tuned their own retries)?

The support driver is real (SUP-9334: TS retry storms on 429; SUP-9321: python streaming hang/timeout confusion). But I don’t want a bunch of “why did my client suddenly retry” tweets.

Can you propose:
- A semver decision for each SDK (py/ts/go) if you think they differ
- A release note / blog-style snippet we can use
- Whether we should ship a “legacy mode” toggle for one release window

If it helps: Ibrahim says spec is aiming for “safe retries by default” w/ strict budgets + honoring Retry-After.

— Nikhil
Product, Hosted API


From: Henry Cho <henry@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: SDK parity rollout — release messaging + semver (defaults vs flags)

My take (product messaging + “minimize customer pain”):

Semver
- Retry/timeout *default* changes are effectively behavioral breaking for some customers, but we can usually keep semver minor if:
  (a) we keep public API surface compatible, and
  (b) we give an explicit escape hatch + callouts.
- Streaming disconnect handling is the touchiest; if we change from “best effort reconnect” to “fail-fast + surface partial” (or vice versa) that’s where customers notice.

Recommendation
- Ship as minor releases across py/ts/go, with a temporary “legacy behavior” toggle for one minor cycle (e.g., env var or client option). Deprecate toggle immediately; remove in the next minor.
- Avoid per-feature flags. One unified toggle is easier to explain.

Proposed toggle naming
- Something like REDWOOD_SDK_BEHAVIOR=legacy|standard (default: standard) OR client option: behavior: 'standard'|'legacy'.

Messaging
- Frame as reliability + predictability: “SDKs now behave consistently across languages. Retries and timeouts are safer by default and respect rate limits.”
- Explicitly note budgets: max attempts, jitter, Retry-After honored, no retries on non-idempotent streaming.

I can draft release notes + a short FAQ section for docs. Will share later today.

— Henry


From: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:17 PM PT
Subject: Re: SDK parity rollout — release messaging + semver (defaults vs flags)

A few technical constraints that should inform the semver + messaging:

1) Retries
- Standard is NOT “retry everything.”
- Retryable: 429 + selected 5xx + transient transport (connection reset, DNS) with a small max attempt count + retry budget.
- Honor Retry-After when present, and include request-id propagation.
- Default will be less aggressive than TS today (this is a net reduction in retries for the ticket we saw).

2) Streaming
- We are standardizing to: no automatic reconnect/resume for SSE streams (cannot guarantee idempotency; partial output semantics).
- On mid-stream disconnect: surface a typed error that includes whether any tokens were received; caller decides what to do.

3) Timeouts
- Clarify that streaming has “no overall timeout by default” but has read idle timeout (or keepalive-based) so we don’t hang forever behind proxies.

Re: “legacy toggle”
- I’m fine with a single global behavior toggle *if* it doesn’t become a long tail. Agree: deprecate immediately and time-box.

Also: we should avoid a toggle that looks like it bypasses rate limits. We should be very clear retries respect rate limits.

— Ibrahim


From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>, Henry Cho <henry@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 2:03 PM PT
Subject: Re: SDK parity rollout — release messaging + semver (defaults vs flags)

+1 to minor releases with a time-boxed escape hatch.

Two requirements from DevEx side:
- We cannot ship “surprise majors” in all three SDKs simultaneously. It will blow up docs + examples + adoption.
- Whatever we do must be extremely explicit in quickstarts (Wei/Elliot) so new users see the standard behavior and don’t copy old snippets.

Proposed practical approach:
- Minor release for each SDK that flips defaults to standard behavior.
- Provide legacy toggle for ONE release window (e.g., 60 days) and document it as a temporary migration aid.
- Add a console/app log warning when legacy toggle is used (without spamming; once per process). This helps support.

Nikhil/Henry — please make sure release notes include: “Why we changed defaults” and “How to keep old behavior temporarily.”

— Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Developer Experience
Redwood Inference


From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
To: Henry Cho <henry@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:41 AM PT
Subject: Re: SDK parity rollout — release messaging + semver (defaults vs flags)

Thanks all. I’m aligned on:
- Minor releases (not majors)
- One global legacy toggle, time-boxed

Open items we need to lock today:
A) Toggle name + exact contract (env var vs client option vs both)
B) How we describe streaming disconnect change without implying “we used to auto-reconnect safely”
C) Semver language in changelogs (“behavior change” vs “breaking change”)

Henry — can you share the draft notes/FAQ when ready? I want to route through PM-611 and get Connor to line up timing.

Ibrahim — for the doc snippet: can you give 2-3 crisp bullets on what’s retryable and what’s NOT (especially streaming)?

— Nikhil


From: Henry Cho <henry@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 1:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: SDK parity rollout — release messaging + semver (defaults vs flags)

Draft is here: Release_notes_draft_SDK_parity_v0.3 (link)

Answers / proposal:

A) Toggle contract
- Support both env var + client option (env var is easiest for ops rollbacks).
- Env var: REDWOOD_SDK_BEHAVIOR=legacy|standard
- Client option: behavior: 'legacy' | 'standard' (takes precedence over env var)
- Default: standard
- Deprecation note: “legacy supported until 2025-04-01” (or “60 days from release”, Connor can set exact date)

B) Streaming messaging
- “Streaming reconnection/resume is not enabled by default because token streams are not safely resumable.”
- “If a stream disconnects mid-response, the SDK surfaces a StreamingDisconnected error; applications can decide whether to retry the full request.”

C) Semver language
- Changelog: “Behavioral changes” section + “Migration” section.
- Call out as “may be breaking if you relied on prior defaults.” (We should not label as “Breaking change” unless we actually bump major.)

Notes on tone
- Lead with benefits: fewer hangs, fewer retry storms, consistent behavior across languages.
- Include a one-liner: “If you previously configured custom retries/timeouts, you can keep your settings; the SDK will not override explicit config.”

Let me know if you want this compressed further for GitHub releases.

— Henry


From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Henry Cho <henry@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Ibrahim Khan <ibrahim@redwoodinference.com>, Wei Chen <wei@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 5:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: SDK parity rollout — release messaging + semver (defaults vs flags)

Locking proposal for release train (unless objections by EOD tomorrow):

- Ship minor releases:
  - Python: 1.18.0
  - TypeScript: 2.6.0
  - Go: 0.14.0 (still pre-1.0, but we’ll treat it like semver minor for comms)
- Legacy behavior toggle supported through Apr 1, 2025; removal planned in following minor.
- Docs/quickstarts merged before SDK tags (docs PR 904 + quickstarts PR 233).

Action items
- Henry: finalize release note wording + FAQ by Monday; I’ll paste into GitHub releases.
- Wei/Elliot: ensure quickstart snippets include recommended timeout config + mention behavior toggle only in migration section (not in primary path).
- Ibrahim/Monica: confirm that “no stream auto-resume” line matches ADR-0138 language.

Tracking under PM-611 + ENG-2481.

— Connor
Release Coordination
Redwood Inference
